# 0023. A .NET client generated by Kiota

Status: Accepted

## Context

A presentation that runs on the user's machine, a desktop app or a WebAssembly app, calls the API
over HTTP, as [ADR 0022](0022-a-presentation-project-reaches-the-core-through-the-api-or-the-application-layer.md)
has it. Types written by hand drift from what the API returns, and each such app would solve the
same problems its own way: the base address, transient failures, the session and its refresh, and
reading a problem's `code`. The reviewed OpenAPI reference already describes every route, contract
and problem answer, `code` and field errors included.
<!--#if (anyWeb)-->
This is [ADR 0019](0019-one-generated-api-client.md) for .NET: one generated client and one thin
wrapper, the same for every app.
<!--#endif-->

## Decision

- **One project of the presentation layer, `src/Presentation/AT.Presentation.Client`, generated by
  Kiota.** A client of the API is a presentation concern: only presentation hosts call it, so it sits
  beside `src/Presentation/AT.Presentation.Core`, its tests beside theirs, and the architecture keeps
  its four layers. `Generated/` is what Kiota writes from `tests/Integration/AT.Api.IntegrationTests/OpenApi/v1.json`: the
  `ApiClient` class in `AppTemplate.Presentation.Client.Generated`, with `--exclude-backward-compatible`.
  `dotnet cleanarch openapi` writes it with the Kiota the tool manifest pins, adds the
  BOM the C# files carry here, and writes `kiota-lock.json` with the reference's relative path.
  The output is committed.
- **Drift fails.** `openapi --check` regenerates into a temporary folder and fails on any
  difference; `verify` runs it.
<!--#if (ci)-->
  CI runs it on every pull request.
<!--#endif-->
- **The generated code is generated code.** Every file opens with Kiota's `// <auto-generated/>`
  header and `.editorconfig` marks `**/Generated/**.cs` as generated, so the analyzers and
  `dotnet format` leave it alone. Kiota writes `#pragma warning disable CS0618` and `CS1591` in each
  file, with or without `--exclude-backward-compatible`; those lines stay in `Generated/`, and no
  hand-written file carries one. The layout rules read `Generated/` as generated, and
  `coverage.runsettings` leaves it out of the measure.
- **A wrapper no larger than the problems it solves**, in `Common/`. `ApiClientFactory.Create`
  builds the client over an `HttpClient`, with an `IAccessTokenProvider` when a token comes from
  elsewhere. `AddApiClient` registers it through `IHttpClientFactory` with the standard resilience
  handler. `ApiSession` holds the access token in memory, refreshes once on a `401` for all the
  calls waiting on it and replays each; the refresh token stays in an `IRefreshTokenStore`, in
  memory by default and sent in the body, or in the browser's cookie through
  `X-Refresh-Token-Mode: cookie`. `ApiProblem.From` reads a problem's `code`, detail and field
  errors from the typed `ProblemDetails` and `ValidationProblemDetails`; an answer that is no
  problem document, or one without a `code`, becomes `response.unreadable`, so a caller branches on
  codes alone.
- **A client reaches the core through the API alone.** The client references no project, and a
  presentation that calls the API through it references the client alone, though other presentation
  projects may reference the application layer.
  `EveryClient_ReachesTheCoreThroughTheApiAlone` holds both, by the client's project name rather than
  by its folder.

## Alternatives considered

- **NSwag.** Its C# output does not build here: the multipart file parameter type is missing, the
  client is one file of thousands of lines, and its JSON converter reads types by reflection, which
  trimming breaks.
- **Refitter.** A third-party generator over Refit, with telemetry on by default, a reflection-based
  converter, and problems parsed by hand.
- **Types written by hand.** Each contract change would have to be copied by hand, and nothing
  would say when one was missed.
- **A layer folder of its own, beside the four.** It would read as a fifth layer of the
  architecture, though nothing but a presentation host calls it, and the rule that keeps it from
  the core needs no folder: it names the project.
- **The client inside `Presentation.Core`.** That project references the application layer, so a
  desktop or WebAssembly app that took the client from it would ship the server's code and could
  reach the use cases in process.

## Consequences

- A change to the API's contract is a compile error in every .NET client that relied on the old
  one, once `openapi` has run.
- The session's refresh goes through an `HttpClient` of its own, without the resilience handler: a
  rotated refresh token presented twice would end the session.
- A status the contract does not declare for a route reads as `response.unreadable`, since Kiota
  maps a problem to its type by the declared status.
- Kiota and `Microsoft.Kiota.Bundle` move together: Dependabot opens them in one pull request, and
  `openapi` regenerates the output against the new version.

## Revisit when

Kiota stops writing the `#pragma` lines or the header, a client needs a transport Kiota does not
generate, or the client must leave the solution as a package of its own.
